assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks turned a clever idea (magic-wavelength trapping of many atoms, free of Doppler and recoil shifts) into the most precise measurements ever made, at the 10^-18 level. This is quantum mechanics of atoms controlled and understood to the last digit, and the result opens tests of fundamental constants and relativistic time dilation across centimetres. It is the kind of precision atomic physics I trust.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and realised the strontium lattice clock; Ye's group brought it to the 10^-18 regime and demonstrated the gravitational redshift over millimetre scales. Both are clearly decisive. Other groups (e.g. Lemonde, Ludlow, Hinkley, Bloom) contributed, and the two-name credit cannot cover all of them, but the core is reasonable.
assessment.maturity: Many independent laboratories worldwide operate lattice clocks and agree with each other; redefinition of the second is under discussion. Mature and confirmed, and timely, with the 2005 comb prize and 2012 ion-trap prize already giving context.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes (frequency combs, Hall and Hansch; Wineland's ion clocks) could make the committee feel the area is already honoured.
Allocation of credit among Katori, Ye, Lemonde and others is not fully settled; I rely on general knowledge here and have not verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices became a clean, tunable laboratory for the Hubbard model and for strongly correlated quantum matter, for example the observation of the superfluid to Mott insulator transition and later single-site imaging. It says something new about how many-body quantum systems behave, and I find it conceptually elegant.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch and collaborators) provided the theoretical proposal and Bloch's group the leading experimental programme, including the 2002 Mott transition work with Greiner. Esslinger and Cirac are also strong and the five-name credit exceeds the three-laureate limit, so a choice must be made, which will be contentious. The proposed three are my best combination of theory and experiment.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups, widely built upon, and now a mature field. Timely.
uncertainties: Selecting three of five credited people is difficult and may omit essential contributors (Esslinger, Cirac, Hansch group for the original Mott experiment).
Overlap with the 2001 BEC and 2012 prizes needs to be weighed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Aharonov-Bohm effect and Berry phase say something deep about the role of gauge potentials and geometry in quantum mechanics, and exactly the sort of boundary between mathematical structure and observable physics I like. The concepts underlie topological phases, Born-Oppenheimer physics and quantum computation.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov and Bohm (1959) predicted the effect, but David Bohm has died, so the living credit is limited; Berry's 1984 phase was partly anticipated by earlier work (Pancharatnam, Mead and Truhlar, Aharonov and Anandan). Credit is a real problem, and the two-name configuration is only defensible if the committee accepts the omission of Bohm.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed for decades (Chambers, Tonomura, optics and NMR demonstrations of Berry phase). Very mature, perhaps even overdue.
uncertainties: Bohm's death and the partial priority of others for the geometric phase complicate a fair prize.
The two achievements are separate discoveries, so it could be seen as a combined prize of loosely connected parts.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Making strongly interacting Fermi gases and mapping the BEC-BCS crossover tested fermionic pairing in a system we can control and compare with theory in detail. It connects to superconductivity, neutron stars and nuclear matter, and gives the universal behaviour at unitarity.
assessment.attribution: Thomas's early unitary gas, Grimm and Salomon on molecular BEC and pair condensates, with important simultaneous work from Jin, Ketterle and Zwierlein that is not in the credited list. The configuration omits those and may therefore not stand on its own.
assessment.maturity: Robust and multiply reproduced, theory and experiment agree closely. Mature and not premature.
uncertainties: Missing the Jin (deceased) and Ketterle/Zwierlein contributions makes this three-name credit questionable; the credit configuration is unresolved.
Ketterle already received the 2001 prize, which may weaken the case.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made it possible to study strong light-matter coupling with artificial atoms on a chip, a direct engineering of the quantum optics I know, and the foundation for superconducting quantum computers. The 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits makes this a natural follow-up.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Girvin, Huang, Wallraff, Schoelkopf wrote the 2004 proposal and first experiments; four are credited, and I pick the theorist who led the proposal and the two main experimentalists. Girvin's omission is a loss.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed and used worldwide; but the recent 2025 prize may suggest waiting.
uncertainties: The close timing with the 2025 prize may argue against immediate recognition of the same broad field.
Credit among the proposal's authors is shared and my selection leaves out Girvin.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Higgs discovery was a central result, but the 2013 prize already honoured the theory. The experimental conception and construction of ATLAS and CMS is an extraordinary achievement and gives a measured completion of the Standard Model.
assessment.attribution: Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee are the commonly named founders of the collaborations; spokespersons of the 2012 discovery are separate people. I defer to the particle physics members regarding fairness of crediting leaders of collaborations of thousands.
assessment.maturity: The discovery is solidly confirmed and properties measured by two experiments. Mature but already partly recognised.
uncertainties: The 2013 prize already recognised the Higgs mechanism; whether an experimental award is necessary is for particle-physics colleagues.
Credit for large collaborations is intrinsically hard to allocate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect are a genuinely new class of matter with robust edge states, theoretically predicted and then observed. I recognise their significance but I defer to my condensed matter colleagues on the finer balance.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction; Molenkamp's group observed the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe following Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang's proposal, which is not credited here, and Hasan observed the 3D materials. The best three here are Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, but Zhang (deceased) and Hasan have strong claims.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by several experiments and now widely developed; very mature after the 2016 Thouless, Haldane, Kosterlitz prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 topological-phase prize and unresolved credit among Hasan, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Molenkamp.
Condensed matter is outside my main expertise.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry uses the wave nature of massive atoms for precision measurements of gravity, rotation and tests of the equivalence principle. It is conceptually clear and relates to my own field.
assessment.attribution: Bordé, Pritchard and Kasevich pioneered the field; Chu's work is separate and he already has a prize, and Schmiedmayer is also credited, so four names compete for three places.
assessment.maturity: Well-established, with many laboratories and increasing practical application, but the biggest tests are still improving; recognition is plausible now but the scientific peak may be ahead.
uncertainties: Earlier prizes for laser cooling (Chu, Cohen-Tannoudji, Phillips) and for Ramsey's separated-field method may blur how credit is allocated.
Four candidate names; the exclusion of Schmiedmayer is not strongly justified.
